scores.evidence: Yjs converges for our schema; its leftover deleted-content markers ("tombstones") stay within the storage and load budgets
scores.rationale: Technology claims (Yjs/ProseMirror/Hocuspocus, tombstone overhead, ack-after-durable-commit, consistent hashing, RLS) are accurate throughout, and library guarantees are treated as assumptions to validate rather than asserted.

scores.evidence: A browser-based rich-text editor where several people edit the same document at once. Each person's edits show up for the others live
scores.rationale: Covers the core collaborative-editing needs with explicit, justified deferrals, but collaborative undo is neither included nor explicitly excluded, a minor gap in an otherwise precise fit.

scores.evidence: The server acks only after a durable Postgres commit; the UI shows "unsaved" until then
scores.rationale: Decisions made once (durability semantics, one owning server per doc, tenancy, privacy boundary) are honored consistently across phases, validation gates and cross-cutting tables with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: Property-based fuzz testing: 3–10 simulated clients with random reorder, duplication, delay and partition, 1M generated edit sequences
scores.rationale: Each validation (V0–V5) targets a specific risk with checkable thresholds labeled as assumptions, runs before the dependent commitment, and production monitoring (convergence checksum, divergence alerts) continues post-launch.

scores.evidence: UNKNOWN: needs projected peak concurrent editors and open docs. Product owner supplies it in Phase 1
scores.rationale: Assumptions and unknowns are explicitly labeled, each has a confirmation path, and sensitivity is stated (E2EE restarts the plan, offline-first pulls storage into Phase 1).

scores.evidence: Chaos tests under load: kill the owning server mid-edit, rolling deploy, dropped connections, Postgres failover
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures — silent divergence, lost acked edits, revocation mid-session, cross-tenant leaks, malicious input, duplicates — each with concrete detection (checksum, canaries) and recovery.

scores.evidence: Two deployables, managed Postgres, Redis only if V4 flips; ≤ 2 pages/week
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback, drain/handover, expand/contract migrations, meaningful alerts and an explicit on-call budget sized to a ≤6-engineer team are all designed in from Phase 0.

scores.evidence: GA infrastructure commitment and pricing [depends on] Cost per open document-hour, measured in V4
scores.rationale: Storage growth, per-doc-hour run cost and build-vs-buy trade-offs are grounded and gated on measurement, but build-side people cost and absolute magnitudes are thin.

scores.evidence: R3: it fixes the stored format and the client protocol; real docs cannot be safely re-encoded
scores.rationale: Every decision is classified by reversibility with revisit triggers, irreversible ones are validated before real documents exist, and the point of no return is explicitly marked.

scores.evidence: Several servers per doc (Redis fan-out): pulled forward when V4 fails or a doc needs more than 50 editors
scores.rationale: Two deployables and managed services are the simplest workable design for this domain, with every added component justified and speculative scale explicitly deferred with pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: If V1 fails: switch to OT and delete the disposable docs
scores.rationale: Phases have ordered concrete tasks, dependency reasoning, checkable exit criteria, and explicit adaptation paths if validations fail, so a team could start immediately.

Minimal Tiptap schema (paragraphs, headings, lists, marks, links, images by reference), versioned, with migrate-on-load

Postgres append-only edit log plus snapshots... Ack only after a durable commit... Compact the edit history into snapshots

presence (live cursors) via Yjs awareness, which is temporary and not saved

50 editors in one doc, plus the whole-system mix at 2× projected peak... Unload idle docs from server memory
tenant_id and schema_version on every row... versioned, with migrate-on-load... Schema-migration tests on a synthetic set of docs
